applied.problem: It says a bigger coil changes only τ and the input alone sets the steady value; a real bigger coil usually has more winding resistance, E ÷ R depends on R, and after i7 a pushed spring's steady swing depends on the system too, not only the push (the quote says independent of the start).

The mistake 'expecting a bigger coil to change the final current' is often right in real life, since a bigger coil usually has more winding resistance; only more L with the same R leaves E ÷ R unchanged.

Screen 9's 'whatever the settings, 0.368 at every τ mark' fails across a mid-run switch flip, where the steady line and gap jump; and screen 11's 'percentage of its steady value' matches 63.2% at one τ only for a start from zero, while 'share of the way' holds for any start.
